1:
Let $t$ be hours after midnight. Min $20$ at $t=5$, max $70$ at $t=16$: half-period 11 h, period 22 h, midline 45, amplitude 25. Starting at the minimum:
\[T(t)=45-25\cos\!\Big(\frac{2\pi}{22}(t-5)\Big).\]
$T>59\iff\cos\!\big(\frac{2\pi}{22}(t-5)\big)<-0.56$. With $\alpha=\cos^{-1}(-0.56)\approx2.1652$ and $\omega=\frac{2\pi}{22}$:
\[t-5\in\Big(\frac{\alpha}{\omega},\ \frac{2\pi-\alpha}{\omega}\Big)=(7.582,\ 14.418)\ \Rightarrow\ t\in(12.58,\ 19.42).\]
The next such interval starts at $t\approx34.6$, after the first 26 hours. Total: \boxed{\approx6.84\ \text{hours}}.
2:
Let $t$ be years after 1998 and $H(t)=\dfrac{at+b}{ct+1}$. It never exceeds 120 and increases toward it, so $\frac{a}{c}=120$, i.e. $a=120c$. $H(0)=55\Rightarrow b=55$.

$H(8)=78$: $\dfrac{960c+55}{8c+1}=78\Rightarrow 960c+55=624c+78\Rightarrow c=\frac{23}{336}\approx0.06845$, $a\approx8.214$.

Set $H(t)=100$: $120ct+55=100ct+100\Rightarrow 20ct=45\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{45}{20c}=\dfrac{45\cdot336}{460}\approx\boxed{32.87\ \text{years after 1998}}$.
3:
In 32 s he runs $4(32)=128$ m of arc. The angle is $\theta=\frac{128}{50}=2.56$ rad (less than one lap). The straight-line distance is the chord:
\[d=2r\sin\frac{\theta}{2}=100\sin(1.28)\approx\boxed{95.80\ \text{m}}.\]
4:
Break the line at every point where either rule changes: $0$, $4$, $5$.
\begin{itemize}
\item $x<0$: $2x+(-3x)=-x$
\item $0\le x\le4$: $2x+(x-2)=3x-2$
\item $4<x<5$: $2x+(-x)=x$
\item $x\ge5$: $-5x+(-x)=-6x$
\end{itemize}
\[h(x)=\begin{cases}-x, & x<0\\ 3x-2, & 0\le x\le4\\ x, & 4<x<5\\ -6x, & x\ge5\end{cases}\]
(These match the final answers on Prof. Conroy's posted key, Version A.)
